expectedPlan.for: Niagara: 41,809 proposals in 21 reviewed packages, area revision 0
expectedPlan.packageRead: Seq Scan on import_packages filtered by area_id (no area index; the table holds tens of rows), top-N sort to 30; per package one detoast of its body and one jsonb_array_elements/jsonb_agg pass building 41,809 five-field objects (about 8 to 10 MB of JSON to the API); then assertAreaPackageAuthority per package (a few primary-key reads of sources each)
expectedPlan.rule: one read of id and revision for the area's physical_features rows (41,809 rows; no area_id index, so a sequential scan), then one sources read and documentAuthorityTx per package with candidates (21)
expectedPlan.window: Append of two branches, then Sort by identifier and Limit limit+1. Recorded: Bitmap Index Scan on physical_geographic_gist for ST_Intersects(f.geographic_geometry, win.g), with membership, the cursor and f.id <> ALL(chosen) (a hashed array test on PostgreSQL 15 and later) as filters. Proposed: Index Scan on import_packages_pkey for the 21 package ids, a lateral jsonb_array_elements of each body (41,809 elements), Hash Join with the unnest of the 41,809 chosen pairs, Index Scan on physical_features_pkey per chosen feature for its identifier, then ST_GeomFromGeoJSON and ST_Intersects of each proposal's geometry against win.g with no index, because the rows hold no geometry until recorded.
expectedPlan.summary: the same proposed branch with ST_Transform and ST_Extent over the 41,809 geometries, plus the recorded members' sequential pass as before
expectedPlan.expectedSeconds: about 1 to 3 s per window page or summary for Niagara, dominated by the package bodies' expansion and the 41,809 geometry parses; inside the 15 s statement timeout. A window read does this work for every page; the Studio's paging to its 15,000 budget at 2,000 a page is up to 8 such reads.
expectedPlan.why: No PostgreSQL with PostGIS may be started or queried by this task; the plan was not captured with EXPLAIN.

gaps: The proposal branch is not served by a spatial index: until a package is recorded its rows hold no geometry, so every window page parses all chosen proposals' geometry. An indexed path needs the database to hold proposal geometry (a schema change outside this task).
The Studio does not yet read displayState; telling a recorded footprint from a proposal on the map is the Studio owner's step.
Like the context read, the window reads draw from the area's newest 30 packages only.
